correctness.rationale: The graph is the explicit 12-vertex 30-edge icosahedron and a simplex is precisely a set of graph edges extendible to a six-edge perfect matching. Independent least-remaining-vertex enumeration gives 125 perfect matchings, and all nonempty subfaces yield f=(30,315,1260,1575,750,125), 4055 total. Of 1400 three-edge matchings, exactly 140 fail extendability. Independent construction of the deterministic 1977-pair matching and full 15210-incidence DAG leaves (critical C0,C2,C3)=(1,62,38). Exact signed Morse C3→C2 is 38×62 with 240 nonzero entries and absolute entries≤2, and independent integral Smith reduction has nineteen unit factors, zero others. With C1=0, π2(∨62 S²)=Z^62, so the unimodular attaching degrees cancel nineteen C2/C3 pairs, leaving 43 S² and 19 S³. Mod-two only corroborates; integral argument rules out torsion.

originality.rationale: Perfect-matching-extendability complex P(I) is a proper subcomplex of the ordinary matching complex M(I), so the published three-primary-torsion homotopy of M(I) does not compute P(I). Earlier Bayer–Jelić Milutinović–Vega honeycomb and Chandrakar–Singh polygonal-line tiling families omit the triangular icosahedral graph. Plummer 1994 studies matching extendability, but its full text was not inspected, and exact homotopy remains a residual risk. Indexed Resultary published Heawood perfect-matching complex concerns a different graph. No covering exact 43S²∨19S³ theorem located by substantive object/alias searches.

value.rationale: The icosahedron is a canonical highly symmetric matching-covered planar triangulation. The perfect-matching extension condition is natural, and its complex already differs from ordinary matching on 140 minimal three-edge faces despite agreeing on all 315 two-edge matchings; its exact mixed-dimensional, torsion-free integral homotopy quantifies a meaningful structural distinction from the ordinary icosahedral matching complex with Z/3-torsion.
